$comment: Primary-source oracle — blocker cases: results that must be WITHHELD with the missing inputs listed, never guessed. The rule is to withhold rather than guess a missing fact; the cited sources establish why each fact is legally required. Expected values derived independently; never from production code.

irs-p590b-beneficiaries.name: IRS Publication 590-B — IRA Beneficiaries (post-death rules)
irs-p590b-beneficiaries.identifier: The post-death distribution rule depends on the beneficiary category, the owner's date of death, and whether the owner died before or on/after their required beginning date — without these no rule can be selected

irs-rmd-faq-still-working.name: IRS — RMD FAQs (still-working delay until retirement year)
irs-rmd-faq-still-working.identifier: A still-working participant's first RMD year is the year they retire — unknown retirement year means the first RMD year cannot be resolved

usc-402ef.name: 42 U.S.C. §402(e)/(f) — widow(er) benefit requires the survivor's own application/election
usc-402ef.identifier: Entitlement requires that the widow(er) 'has filed application for widow's insurance benefits' (subject to the §402(q) reduction at the chosen start); with no survivor claim age on file the amount depends on an unmade election (withhold, no silent early-claim or FRA default)

cases.description: Inherited IRA with only the beneficiary category on file: the RMD is withheld and the two missing baseline facts are listed.
derivation: Pub 590-B: selecting a post-death rule requires the owner's death date and the before/on-after-RBD status; only 'SPOUSE' is on file.

cases.description: Still-working exception applied in prior years but the retirement year is unknown: the first-RMD-year plan is withheld (never guessed).
derivation: IRS RMD FAQ: the delayed first RMD year is the retirement year; without it the later-of rule cannot resolve.

cases.description: Survivor benefit with no survivor claim age on file: the deceased-record component is withheld (null), not defaulted.
derivation: 42 USC 402(e)/(f): the survivor-claim start is the survivor's own election; the withhold-rather-than-guess rule forbids silently assuming an early claim or FRA.
Expected: the survivor benefit computation returns null (withheld) for the same deceased facts that produce $19,800/yr when the claim age IS on file (see survivor.json rib-lim case).

cases.description: Living-owner RMD rule with no owner age resolvable: withheld listing ['ownerAge'] — a missing age must never default to the most favorable divisor.
derivation: The Table III divisor is indexed by the owner's attained age; defaulting a missing age (e.g. to the trigger age) would silently understate the RMD (withhold rather than guess).
